page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-384-metal is a bare-metal server instance belonging to the c4d server family. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 384 dedicated virtual CPUs and 1536.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a balanced resource distribution of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning with standard general-purpose computing profiles. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external network-attached block storage.

The bare-metal nature of this instance ensures direct access to the underlying hardware without hypervisor overhead, which is beneficial for workloads requiring consistent execution times and high resource density. The absence of local NVMe drives and graphics accelerators represents a design tradeoff, prioritizing raw CPU and memory capacity over local storage speed or hardware-accelerated parallel processing. This makes the server cost-efficient for large-scale, CPU-bound workloads that do not require specialized GPU hardware or high-speed local scratch space.

Appropriate workloads for the c4d-standard-384-metal instance include large-scale enterprise applications, high-density container orchestration, extensive web serving fleets, and general-purpose batch processing. It is also suitable for distributed databases and memory-intensive applications that can leverage the 1536.0 GB memory pool alongside the 384 dedicated vCPUs.
